nar.text: Varzi drove his same old P2 he had raced here the year before, which he had sold back to the Portello works at the end of 1929.
About 60,000 people turned up on Easter Sunday for the event.

The start was rather messy with some cars in the front rows slow away and others behind them trying to take advantage of it but in the end it all sorted up without accidents and Bouriano led the field towards Valmadonna.
The cars of category 2 followed three minutes later except for Premoli, who did not find a gear and stalled his Salmson on the grid.
Nuvolari fails to complete the first lap; mechanical problems on his Alfa Romeo.
End of lap 1: Bouriano leads Ferrari by 26 seconds; Varzi, from the fourth row, third and 34 seconds back.
Minozzi is out after the first lap.
The pace was extremely fast and already after the second lap all previous records had been wiped out.
Bouriano still held a 30 seconds advantage to Varzi, who had overhauled Ferrari.
In the 1100cc class Marret's Salmson leads, with a record second lap of 19m43.8s.
Nenzioni had started well, but after the third lap he had to retire.
Varzi laps in 16m53.6s (113.6 km/h) and is about ten seconds behind Bouriano.
Varzi went past Bouriano at the end of the lap on the start and finish straight in front of the grand stands.
Brivio in fifth position was fastest of the 1500cc cars with a medium speed of 100.3 km/h.
Fagioli, in trouble, retires from the 1100cc class; Clerici is second.
On the fifth lap the course was suddenly hit by a violent summer downpour that in an instant caused confusion among the numerous spectators, who frantically tried to find some shelter.
In the section between Valenza and San Salvatore Bouriano, who was following Varzi closely, lost control of his Bugatti in a corner. The car spun twice before overturning.
Varzi now leads Zanelli by almost two minutes.
After five laps Marret leads the 1100cc class by three minutes from Clerici.
Marret has mechanical trouble; after six laps Clerici is 1m20s behind.
Clerici takes the 1100cc lead from Marret in front of the stands.
Behind them Ferrari took advantage of the rain and the muddy state of the road and closed in on Zanelli's much stronger and faster Bugatti by a minute during the last four laps.
Varzi wins by 2m18s at 108.4 km/h from Zanelli; Ferrari third, Valpreda fourth, Brivio fifth.
Clerici wins the 1100cc class; Marret over 3 1/2 minutes behind.
